description: Assign or initialize values of pore-pressure to all gridpoints in the range.
notes: The Itasca 9.7 page lists 'cutoff' in its 'Primary keywords' line, but the engine rejects 'zone gridpoint pore-pressure cutoff' and re-enumerates the six keywords below (live-probed on MPoint3D 9.7, 2026-09-14). cutoff is a sub-keyword of geometry / head / import / initialize / plane / table, not a primary keyword.
Each primary keyword accepts the shared scalar modifiers add / gradient / local / multiply / vary, plus cutoff <f> and effective <b>.

keywords.name: geometry
keywords.description: Specify the pore-pressure as increasing due to gravity with depth below a geometry surface.

keywords.name: head
keywords.description: Uses head to initialize pore pressure at the gridpoint. Pore-pressure is calculated from the head value.

keywords.name: import
keywords.description: Import values from a file and use the data to assign pore-pressures to a gridpoint.

keywords.name: initialize
keywords.description: Set the pore-pressure values in the gridpoints of the range to f.

keywords.name: plane
keywords.description: Specify the pore-pressure as increasing due to gravity by depth from a single plane.

keywords.name: table
keywords.description: Specify the pore-pressure as increasing due to gravity with depth below a table.

keywords.name: kwd:add
keywords.description: Add the specified value to the existing value.

keywords.name: kwd:gradient
keywords.description: Apply a gradient to the scalar-value provided.

keywords.name: kwd:local
keywords.description: Specify that the value supplied for the keyword is in the local coordinate system.

keywords.name: kwd:multiply
keywords.description: Multiply the existing value by the specified value.

keywords.name: kwd:vary
keywords.description: Apply a linear variation to the scalar-value provided.

keywords.name: kwd:cutoff
keywords.description: Pore-pressure values are not allowed to fall below this cutoff value.

keywords.name: kwd:effective
keywords.description: By default the total stress is held constant, so any change to pore-pressure results in a change to effective stress.
